title: Transcytosis Assay for Transport of Glycosphingolipids across MDCK-II Cells
author: Maria Daniela Garcia-Castillo

steps.title: Plate and seed MDCK‑II cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate growth media from a T‑75 flask of MDCK‑II cells, wash with 5–10 ml warmed sterile PBS, remove PBS, add 3 ml 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 5–10 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, observe detachment, collect suspension, pipet 6–8 times to obtain a homogeneous single‑cell suspension, and seed 200 000 cells in 200 µl complete growth media onto the apical side of each 0.4 µm pore, 12‑well Transwell® insert (65 mm). Add 1 ml complete growth media to the basolateral chamber. Prepare two inserts for untreated control, two for reporter peptide, and two per glycosphingolipid‑peptide fusion (biological duplicates).

steps.title: Polarize cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the seeded Transwell plates for 2–3 days at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified, to allow formation of a polarized monolayer.

steps.title: Verify monolayer integrity
steps.instruction: Measure transepithelial electrical resistance of each insert with an EVOM epithelial voltohmmeter; accept values between 250 Ω and 300 Ω before proceeding.

steps.title: Prepare glycosphingolipid test stock
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lyophilized peptide‑lipid fusion at 13 000 rpm (~13 800 × g) for 3 min, add 1 part DMF (≈60 µl for the typical batch), sonicate in a bath sonicator for 30–60 sec, vortex 5 sec, then add 2 parts H₂O (e.g., 120 µl) and vortex 5 sec to obtain a final 33 % (v/v) DMF/H₂O solution. The resulting stock should be clear bright‑green and have a concentration in the 50–200 µM range (e.g., 100 µg peptide, MW ≈ 2103 Da, dissolved with 50 µl DMF + 100 µl H₂O).

steps.title: Dilute stock to assay concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute an appropriate volume of the 33 % DMF/H₂O stock into Apical Solution (see Recipes) to reach a final concentration of 0.1 µM (maintaining a 1:1 lipid‑to‑dfBSA ratio).

steps.title: Wash and equilibrate Transwells
steps.instruction: Wash each insert twice with serum‑free DMEM, then add 200 µl Apical Solution to the apical chamber and 1 ml Basolateral Solution to the basolateral chamber. Allow the cells to equilibrate for 15 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Add test compounds and incubate
steps.instruction: Replace the apical 200 µl with Apical Solution containing 0.1 µM reporter peptide or 0.1 µM glycosphingolipid‑peptide fusion (stock concentrations 30–150 µM in 33 % DMF/66 % H₂O). Incubate for 3 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Collect media for analysis
steps.instruction: After incubation, collect the basolateral media into pre‑labeled Eppendorf tubes for streptavidin pull‑down, and also collect the apical chamber solution for generation of a standard curve (0–200 nM range).

steps.title: Prepare streptavidin magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Wash Pierce™ Streptavidin magnetic beads three times with 1 ml TBS‑T per wash (gentle inversion, no vortex). Use 10 µl beads per sample (e.g., for 12 samples, place 120 µl beads in a tube, wash, then resuspend in 50 µl TBS). Add the 50 µl bead suspension to each 1 ml basolateral sample.

steps.title: Bind peptides to beads overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the bead‑sample mixtures overnight at 4 °C with head‑over‑rotation, protected from light by foil.

steps.title: Wash beads and elute bound peptide
steps.instruction: Collect beads with a magnetic rack, wash three times with 1 ml TBS‑T (invert to mix each wash). Elute bound peptide by adding 220 µl Elution Buffer (95 % formamide, 10 mM EDTA, 0.4 mg ml⁻¹ biotin), invert, then boil for 2 min at 65 °C. After boiling, re‑collect beads magnetically.

steps.title: Plate eluates and read fluorescence
steps.instruction: Pipet 100 µl of each eluate into two technical replicate wells of a black, flat‑bottom 96‑well plate (no lid). Measure fluorescence on a TECAN Spark microplate reader (Top Reading mode, Excitation 488 nm, Emission 532 nm, Excitation bandwidth 9 nm, Emission bandwidth 20 nm).

steps.title: Generate standard curves
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 µM peptide and lipid‑peptide stocks in Elution Buffer, then make 1 ml of 10 nM solution (10 µl 1 µM + 990 µl buffer). Perform serial dilutions in Elution Buffer as follows: 1000 pM (100 µl 10 nM + 900 µl buffer), 500 pM (500 µl 1000 pM + 500 µl buffer), 250 pM (500 µl 500 pM + 500 µl buffer), 125 pM (500 µl 250 pM + 500 µl buffer), 62.5 pM (500 µl 125 pM + 500 µl buffer), 31.5 pM (500 µl 62.5 pM + 500 µl buffer), 15.6 pM (500 µl 31.5 pM + 500 µl buffer), and 0 pM (buffer only). Use these standards to interpolate sample concentrations.

steps.title: Prepare required solutions (recipes)
steps.instruction:
Prepare the following solutions fresh on the day of assay: 
- MDCK‑II complete growth media: DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1× Pen/Strep. 
- Basolateral solution (40 ml): 40 ml DMEM + 400 mg defatted‑BSA (final 1 % w/v). 
- Apical solution (40 ml): 40 ml DMEM + 24.6 µl Basolateral solution (final df‑BSA ≈0.1 µM). 
- 10× TBS (1 L): 24 g Tris base + 88 g NaCl, dissolve in 900 ml water, adjust pH 7.4, bring to 1 L. 
- 1× TBS‑T (1 L): 100 ml 10× TBS + 1 ml Tween 20 + 900 ml water. 
- 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0 (1 L): dissolve 186.1 g Na₂EDTA in 800 ml water, adjust pH 8.0 with NaOH, bring to 1 L. 
- Elution buffer (100 ml): 95 ml 100 % formamide + 2 ml 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) + 40 mg biotin + 3 ml Milli‑Q water.

description: Materials and Reagents Notes: Material and reagents are stored as per the manufacturer’s recommendation. Fluorescent peptides and glycosphingolipid-peptide fusions are used as described in Garcia-Castillo et al., 2018. The assay requires the presence of both a fluorophore and a biotin covalently attached to compound you want to measure (see Figure 3 ). Peptide fusions containing biotin and fluorophore attached to ganglioside GM1 were synthesized in-house using specialized methods described in (Garcia-Castillo et al., 2018). Precursor peptides were synthesized by New England Peptide (Gardner, MA, USA), and gangliosides were purchased from Dr. Sandro Sonnino (U. Milan, Italy). However, in theory, any macromolecule (peptide, protein, nucleic acid or chemical) containing both a fluorophore and biotin will work in this assay. An example compound is shown below. Here, lower-cased amino acids are depicting D-isomers. Since glycine (shown as upper-cased G) does not have chirality, the peptide essentially contains no L-amino acids that can be susceptible to degradation in vivo. Figure 3.
